text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. When developers make changes to the code, automated builds start immediately. This means the new code is combined with the existing project and checked for problems. During the build, tests run automatically to make sure everything still works correctly. The main benefit of CI is catching issues early, before they become bigger and harder to fix. Teams often set up CI pipelines, which are a series of steps that automatically build, test, and sometimes deploy the code. This saves time and helps developers feel more confident about their work.
